title: Door Pathway
summary: Door Pathway: The Door Pathway centers on freedom of movement: phasing through barriers, travel through the Spirit World, teleportation, and using recorded
searchText: Door Pathway Lord of Mysteries · Standard Pathway Door Pathway Sequence 9: Apprentice → Sequence 0: Door The Door Pathway centers on freedom of movement: phasing through barriers, travel through the Spirit World, teleportation, and using recorded powers. At higher Sequences, it expands into advanced space manipulation, concealment, sealing, precise locating, gravity effects, and alternate-space creation. Pathway progression and late-sequence details contain major story spoilers. Browse the local Door Pathway ingredient archive → Sequence progression Sequence titles are retained from the archive; key ability notes are concise paraphrases of the linked source material. Seq. Name Key abilities 9 Apprentice Opens symbolic doors to phase through ordinary barriers and uses varied ritualistic magic. 8 Trickmaster Uses weak, deceptive spells such as flashes, concealment, elemental tricks, object manipulation, and escape diversions. 7 Astrologer Gains astrology-based divination, divination interference, improved door phasing, and longer-distance escape movement. 6 Scribe Records witnessed active Beyonder powers for limited, weaker single-use replication, with success and capacity constraints. 5 Traveler Navigates the Spirit World, opens long-distance teleportation doors, blinks short distances, and captures objects remotely. 4 Secrets Sorcerer Conceals spaces behind doors, layers illusory doors defensively, hides secrets, exiles targets, and records angel-level powers. 3 Wanderer Wanders through the Astral World and Cosmos, tears space, integrates with environments, and forms spatial cages. 2 Planeswalker Symbolizes self, views distant dimensions, stores scenes as toys, teleports directly, and opens doors to other realms. 1 Key of Stars Manipulates stellar gravity to fragment space, locates targets precisely, and seals through mazes and starlight. 0 Door Commands doors, space, alternate worlds, and seals, enabling world-scale travel, sealing, alternate-world creation, and space destruction. Pathway themes & abilities Its stated concepts are Door, Alternate Worlds, Seals, and Space. Core abilities include Door Opening, Astrology, Ability Recording, Teleportation, Space Manipulation, Concealment, Replication, Sealing, and Locating; the pathway is the main one associated with alternate spaces and illusory worlds, though the article leaves comparison with Sublunary Eye uncertain. Sequence-specific highlights are shown in the progression table above. High-sequence abilities The upper Sequences change the pathway from a specialist discipline into a domain of angelic and divine authority. The highlights below summarize the progression from Sequence 4 upward; details contain major spoilers. Sequences 4–3 Sequence 4 — Secrets Sorcerer: Conceals spaces behind doors, layers illusory doors defensively, hides secrets, exiles targets, and records angel-level powers. Sequence 3 — Wanderer: Wanders through the Astral World and Cosmos, tears space, integrates with environments, and forms spatial cages. Sequences 2–1 Sequence 2 — Planeswalker: Symbolizes self, views distant dimensions, stores scenes as toys, teleports directly, and opens doors to other realms. Sequence 1 — Key of Stars: Manipulates stellar gravity to fragment space, locates targets precisely, and seals through mazes and starlight. Sequence 0 Sequence 0 — Door: Commands doors, space, alternate worlds, and seals, enabling world-scale travel, sealing, alternate-world creation, and space destruction. Sequence highlights are paraphrased from the Lord of the Mysteries Wiki pathway article . Novel lore & story appearances The Door Pathway’s story significance centers on Bethel Abraham (“Mr. Door”), ancestor of the Abraham Family and a powerful Fourth Epoch angel. During the War of the Four Emperors, corruption linked to an Outer Deity led the Evernight Goddess and Lord of Storms to banish him to an isolated space of storms and darkness. His cries reached his descendants and drove many toward madness, obstructing the family’s advancement. Fors Wall and Dorian Gray expose the curse, while Verdu Garcia is manipulated by Amon and Medici into freeing Bethel. Bethel then gives his life to stop the Mother Goddess of Depravity ’s descent, allowing Amon’s apotheosis; the family curse ends Story connections A prestigious family brought low: The Abrahams were major nobles under the Solomon and Tudor regimes, but Bethel’s banishment and maddening calls crippled their Beyonders and contributed to the family’s decline. Dorian Gray later learns that changing allegiance to Mr. Fool can temporarily lift the curse’s effects Fors and Dorian trace the curse: Fors contacts Mr. Door and learns release conditions; Dorian explains the family’s blood curse. Verdu Garcia, seeking to free Bethel, is instead maneuvered by Amon and Medici into performing the release ritual A release becomes an apotheosis crisis: Bethel returns while corrupted and begins advancing; the Mother Goddess of Depravity threatens to enter Earth through him. Bethel accepts self-sacrifice to stop that descent, completing Amon’s route to godhood; the Abraham curse is subsequently removed Figures to know Bethel Abraham / Mr. Door Door-pathway King of Angels and ancestor of the Abraham Family; his banishment is the source of the family’s curse Fors Wall Door-pathway Beyonder who contacts Bethel and conveys the curse’s truth and release solution Dorian Gray Abraham Family member who reveals the blood curse and later receives confirmation that it has ended Verdu Garcia Abraham family member manipulated into the ritual that releases Bethel Amon With Medici, engineers the release; Bethel’s sacrifice enables Amon’s apotheosis Major story spoilers. searchText: Emlyn White Character profile Emlyn White Moon · Sequence 4: Shaman King ( Moon Pathway ) Emlyn White is a Sanguine, a high-ranking deacon in the Harvest Church, and a member of the Tarot Club with the codename The Moon. He, as all Sanguines do, believes in the Moon, or Sanguine Ancestor Lilith. But after being brought to the Harvest Church by Utravsky, he is slowly transferring belief towards Earth Mother. This page includes major-spoiler information from the linked source article. The fact fields below are transcribed from that article’s character infobox. ↑ He got the characteristics by trading with Madam Magician [ 5 ] Translation Language Official Translation English Emlyn White Chinese 埃姆林·怀特 Korean 에믈린 화이트 Thai เอ็มลิน ไวท์ Role & affiliations Aliases and titles The Moon Bai Ailin Affiliations Sanguines Tarot Club Harvest Church Occupation(s) Priest High-ranking Deacon Religion(s) Sanguine Ancestor Lilith Church of the Earth Mother Church of the Fool Pathway & abilities Pathway: Moon Recorded progression: Sequence 4: Shaman King ( Moon Pathway ) Pathway reference Moon Compare sequence names and pathway symbols in the Pathways reference . Quotes 12 lines Complete quote entries transcribed from the character’s dedicated wiki Quotes page. The collection includes available Book One and Book Two entries. What’s wrong with being a vampire? Do you think vampires should be locked up here? Do I have to listen to your nagging and scripture recitals every day? Bullshit, I’m a noble Sanguine, so don’t use such a vulgar name to describe me! — Emlyn to Father Utravsky, Lord of Mysteries , Chapter 315. I only like puppets and pure, beautiful girls! — Emlyn to Sherlock Moriarty, Lord of Mysteries , Chapter 421. Those fellows are really disgraceful. As noble Sanguine, they should sleep in coffins or stay in their own rooms. Why are they mimicking humans and holding all kinds of gatherings? There’s even dancing! — Emlyn in Cosmi's night ball, Lord of Mysteries , Chapter 458. Being a believer because I like ‘Her’ beliefs is completely different from being forcefully turned into a believer through a psychological cue. Even if I do abandon the moon one day and believe in Mother Earth, I also hope that it is a choice that I freely made. It has nothing to do with others; this is the last pride of a Sanguine. — Emlyn White, Lord of Mysteries , Chapter 465. If I really choose to make the attempt, it’s definitely not for myself, but for all Sanguine! Resolving this problem is just an additional perk! — Emlyn to Klein, Lord of Mysteries , Chapter 465. There are indeed differences between professional researchers and amateur enthusiasts, but from this week onwards, I, Emlyn White, would be a professional researcher… Baron Waymandy has never mentioned anything related to the City of Silver, so I can’t ask him directly. As the secret messiah of the Sanguine who is burdened with secrets, I have to be careful in such matters… Attending class for half a day and going to the cathedral for half a day before accompanying the dolls at night seems to be a pretty good life… — Emlyn White, Lord of Mysteries , Chapter 514. One day, I will become a Sanguine Marquis like Lord Nibbs! No, a duke, or even a prince! Only by doing so will I be able to shoulder the responsibility of being the Sanguine’s messiah… Yes, the baron’s remains is only about four thousand pounds; I’ll have a lot of money left. I can even buy a few more dolls and give them some new clothes… — Emlyn White, Lord of Mysteries , Chapter 540. Ahem [...] Ma’am Hermit, I have to emphasize that it’s Sanguine, not Vampire. Heh heh, I won’t object it if you call those humans who consume the characteristics of my kinsmen vampires. I would even be very agreeable to it. — Emlyn to Cattleya , Lord of Mysteries , Chapter 595. This should be why us Sanguine are very handsome and beautiful. — Emlyn White, Lord of Mysteries , Chapter 595. I’m very confident in my intelligence. — Emlyn White, Lord of Mysteries , Chapter 792. I’m already very humble. I didn’t mention I would become a Duke or even a Prince… How am I to be the Sanguine’s messiah without being an angel? — Emlyn's Thought, Lord of Mysteries , Chapter 1009. The dark, silent environment is still alright, but it’s just a little cold… But without dolls, newspapers, books, and historical documents, this life is meaningless… Besides, the Nighthawks provide me with cow blood, and it tastes nasty. The effects aren’t too good either. I’m already becoming weak… — Emlyn's Thought, Lord of Mysteries , Chapter 1129. searchText: Error Pathway Lord of Mysteries · Standard Pathway Error Pathway Sequence 9: Marauder → Sequence 0: Error The Error Pathway governs deception and theft, progressing from stealing physical objects to abilities, thoughts, life, fate, identity, time, and authorities. At high Sequences, its Beyonders use parasitism, avatars, fate manipulation, time manipulation, and rule loopholes to behave like an Error or bug. Pathway progression and late-sequence details contain major story spoilers. Browse the local Error Pathway ingredient archive → Sequence progression Sequence titles are retained from the archive; key ability notes are concise paraphrases of the linked source material. Seq. Name Key abilities 9 Marauder Senses valuable items within ten meters and covertly steals possessions; gains agile hands and short-weapon proficiency. 8 Swindler Uses charm, eloquence, thought misdirection, and mental disruption; can read micro-expressions and steal certain spiritual materials. 7 Cryptologist Decrypts mysteries from fragmentary evidence through enhanced deduction, spiritual intuition, and mysticism knowledge; detects subtle clues. 6 Prometheus Steals Beyonder powers or objects within fifty meters, temporarily uses powers, and senses valuables’ location and type. 5 Dream Stealer Disguises as a deity’s follower to steal prayer responses; steals thoughts, dreams, abilities, attacks, memories, and knowledge. 4 Parasite Uses Worms of Time for parasitism, hosts, and avatars; steals abilities, life aspects, position, and distance. 3 Mentor of Deceit Extends deceit to abstract concepts and reality’s rules, manipulates mystical connections, discerns weaknesses, and steals three powers at once. 2 Trojan Horse of Destiny Exploits loopholes, senses and alters fate, steals identity, self-awareness, characteristics, connections, and up to six powers. 1 Worm of Time Temporarily steals time, anchors, and authorities; manipulates time, ages targets, reverses time briefly, and reads recent history. 0 Error Embodies errors and loopholes, deceives rules, creates bugs, steals authorities, and redirects or avoids attacks through substitutions. Pathway themes & abilities Its core skill is Theft, whose scope becomes increasingly conceptual as the pathway advances; related capabilities include deceit, decryption, parasitism, avatars, fate manipulation, and time control. Its symbolism centers on parasitism, time, and fate, while the highest Sequence embodies loopholes and errors in rules. Sequence-specific highlights are shown in the progression table above. High-sequence abilities The upper Sequences change the pathway from a specialist discipline into a domain of angelic and divine authority. The highlights below summarize the progression from Sequence 4 upward; details contain major spoilers. Sequence 3 — Mentor of Deceit: Extends deceit to abstract concepts and reality’s rules, manipulates mystical connections, discerns weaknesses, and steals three powers at once. Amon, a child of the Ancient Sun God and a Third Epoch King of Angels, became Sequence 0 Error by replacing Mr. Door in the apotheosis ritual; after Klein defeated him, Amon revived through an avatar and departed for the cosmos. In Volume 6, Amon captures Klein and attempts to entice him into surrendering his destiny. Pallez Zoroast 's history then shows Amon's conflict reaching Leonard's circle: a trap tied to the Jacob Family treasure costs Pallez his Sequence 1 status Story connections Klein vs. Amon: Amon holds Klein captive during the journey into the Forsaken Land of the Gods and tries to win Klein's destiny; the volume summary records Klein's escape with the Evernight Goddess's help Amon vs. Pallez: Pallez's attempt to recover using the Jacob Family's secret treasure turns out to be Amon's trap, and Pallez loses his Sequence 1 characteristic Error's pathway succession: Amon replaces Mr. Door in the apotheosis ritual to become Sequence 0 Error, then accommodates the Door Uniqueness; these events bind the Error and Door lineages in the story Figures to know Amon Error-pathway King of Angels and the central antagonist in the Klein conflict Klein Moretti Amon's captive in Volume 6 and the one who eventually defeats him Pallez Zoroast Error angel who parasitizes Leonard Mitchell and loses his Sequence 1 characteristic to Amon Leonard Mitchell Pallez's host and student; Pallez becomes his mentor while residing in him Major story spoilers. searchText: Eternal Aeon Pathway Non-Standard Pathway · Circle of Inevitability Eternal Aeon Pathway Outer Deity: Circle of Inevitability · Boon advancement The Eternal Aeon pathway, also called the Dancer or Inevitability pathway, represents predetermined and decisive fate. It specializes in ritual dances, contracts, fate prediction, fate manipulation, and accumulating power from other beings. The Circle of Inevitability grants its Earth-side advancement through Boons rather than standard potions. Non-standard pathway lore and Outer Deity corruption details contain major story spoilers. Browse the local Eternal Aeon Pathway ingredient archive → High-level abilities The pathway’s upper abilities are inseparable from the corruption of its Outer Deity. These powers are expressed through Boons, mystical influence, and the gradual replacement of ordinary cause-and-effect with the pathway’s domain. Anchors a chosen tributary of the River of Fate so that interference with a designated project becomes increasingly doomed to fail. Uses Cycle and Loop to reset regions, undo developments, and force events or battles to repeat. Fixes a person’s fate onto madness or suffering, preserving the body while turning the future into a predetermined catastrophe. Uses Substitution to replace figures in the River of Fate, switch bodies or identities, and create profound mystical links for pursuit. Corruption from Circle of Inevitability The Circle of Inevitability is the pathway’s Outer Deity and primary source of Boons. Corruption can appear as physical mutation, mental contamination, altered fate, environmental collapse, or the rewriting of reality, depending on the pathway’s authority. title: Fifth Epoch
summary: A spoiler-marked guide to the Fifth Epoch of Lord of the Mysteries: the Iron Age, Roselle's Industrial Revolution, colonization, the World War, and the rise of the modern era.
searchText: Fifth Epoch ↑ World chronology · major spoilers Fifth Epoch The Iron Age—an era of industry, empires, colonialism, war, and the slow creep of an approaching apocalypse. The Fifth Epoch, more commonly known as the Iron Age , began roughly 1349 years before the start of the novel. With the gods weakened after the Conflicts of the Seven Gods, humanity slowly rebuilds from the ruins of the Fourth Epoch, ushering in a new age of steam, gunpowder, and rapid change. Major spoilers for Lord of the Mysteries and Circle of Inevitability follow. Epoch timeline The timeline below follows the simplified chronology used across the archive, referencing events leading up to and during the modern era. Year 1349 AE of the Fifth Epoch is the year of Zhou Mingrui's arrival as Klein Moretti . Key periods of the Fifth Epoch Period Years (AE) Relative to novel start Notes Rebuilding 0–359 1349–990 BA Seven Orthodox Churches and Four Great Nations rise; secret organizations proliferate. Regional Wars 359–738 990–611 BA Twenty-Year War, White Rose War, and growing tensions between Churches. Battle of the Violated Oath 738–? ~611 BA onward Religious conflict splits Feynapotter; Lenburg, Masin, Segar gain independence. Centralization & Stagnation 870–1055 479–294 BA Gunpowder spreads, wars become localized, mysticism is dismissed as myth. Roselle & Industrial Revolution 1173–1198 176 BA – 151 BA Steam engine, colonization routes, Cards of Blasphemy, rise and fall of the Intis Empire. Colonization Era ~1194 onward 155 BA onward Southern Continent divided; Sonia Sea islands colonized. Pre-World War Late 13th–early 14th century AE ~150–10 BA Great power rivalry; tensions build towards global conflict. World War ~1349 BA era context / around modern ~0–9 AE (novel-adjacent) All-out war engulfs the Northern Continent. Post-War / Lord of Mysteries 1349–1350 AE 0–1 AE Novel start; the apocalyptic pressure of the Outer Deities intensifies. Year 1349 AE is used as the novel start reference (BA = Before Arrival). Overview After the devastation of the Fourth Epoch, the world enters a long period of rebuilding. Gods no longer openly descend, and while the Seven Orthodox Churches remain powerful, their influence is tempered by rising nations and the slow march of secular change. In the shadows, secret organizations, cults, and hidden orders continue to pursue the path of Beyonders. What defines the Iron Age most is progress. Through Roselle Gustav's inventions and the spread of steam power, the Northern Continent undergoes an Industrial Revolution that reshapes society. Nations expand overseas, carving up the Southern Continent and the Sonia Sea for resources and territory. However, this prosperity is built on blood, exploitation, and the ever-growing tension between the Great Powers. As the barrier between reality and the cosmos weakens, the gaze of the Outer Deities turns back to the world. Boon Recipients multiply, ancient seals fray, and by the time of the novel, the Fifth Epoch finds itself on the brink of another cataclysm. Early Fifth Epoch (0–359 AE) Years 0–359 The Fifth Epoch begins more than 1300 years before the events of the story. In the Northern Continent, the Seven Orthodox Churches and the Four Great Nations establish a new order. While public life is dominated by the churches and nation-states, a vast network of secret organizations operates in the shadows, many of them devoted to the mystic arts. In the Southern Continent, the fall of Death leads to upheaval. The Resistance emerges, and kingdoms such as the Highlands Kingdom and the Paz Kingdom are founded in the power vacuum left behind. New esoteric groups also take root during this period, including the Theosophy Order, the Life School of Thought, and the Blood Sanctify Sect. Twenty-Year War and White Rose War 359–624 AE Conflict between the Great Powers dominates the middle centuries. The Loen Kingdom and the Feysac Empire clash in the Twenty-Year War (359–624 AE), ending in Loen's defeat and the loss of Sonia Island. Not long after, the White Rose War erupts between Loen and Intis. This time, Loen emerges victorious and regains its former prestige. During this period of rising nationalism and religious tension, the Church of the Earth Mother and the Church of Wisdom grow increasingly divided, their split hastened by the machinations of other Orthodox Gods. Battle of the Violated Oath 738 AE Longstanding friction between the Church of the Earth Mother and the Church of Wisdom in Feynapotter erupts into open conflict. Loen and Intis intervene under the pretense of protecting religious freedom, drawing Feysac into the war in an attempt to contain the situation. The war lasts five years and is remembered as the Battle of the Violated Oath , as both sides accuse the other of breaking their solemn vows from the end of the Fourth Epoch. In its aftermath, Lenburg, Masin, and Segar gain independence along Loen and Intis' borders with Feynapotter and become strongholds of the Church of Wisdom. The Church of the Earth Mother is left as the sole faith of the Feynapotter Kingdom. 870–1055 AE A Period of Relative Peace Central authority strengthens across the Northern Continent. Large-scale wars subside in favor of smaller, localized conflicts. Gunpowder becomes widespread, bringing profound changes to warfare. Peace and technological advancement lead many to believe the supernatural is mere myth or legend, and pre-Fifth Epoch history is relegated to fairy tales in the eyes of the public. Roselle and the Industrial Revolution 1173–1198 AE "There are some things that make it easier to be ‘infected’ the more you know." The Fifth Epoch's greatest turning point comes with the transmigration of Huang Tao into the body of Roselle Gustav . Blessed with the memories of his previous life and the power of the Savant pathway, Roselle drives the continent into the Industrial Revolution. He invents the steam engine, improves sailing vessels, and creates countless other innovations born from his modern knowledge. The new steamships and improved trade routes give rise to a golden age of commerce and piracy. The God of Craftsmanship rebrands himself as the God of Steam and Machinery to align with this new era of progress. In 1173, Roselle overthrows the Intis Kingdom and becomes consul of the Intis Republic. Through a series of victories, he transforms the Republic into the Intis Empire and crowns himself Caesar the Great in 1192. That same year, he drafts the Civil Code, invents Tarot cards and poker, and creates the Cards of Blasphemy containing the twenty-two Pathways. Roselle also dispatches expeditions in search of the Forsaken Land of the Gods and the Western Continent, and in 1194, he discovers a safe sea route to the Southern Continent—igniting the age of colonization. In 1198, he is assassinated in the White Maple Palace by the Church of the Eternal Blazing Sun alongside much of the former Sauron royal family. Though he had ascended to Sequence 0 Black Emperor with the aid of the Twilight Hermit Order, his resurrection fails, and the Uniqueness and Characteristics are reclaimed. In the decades that follow, organizations such as the Element Dawn, the Iron and Blood Cross Order, and the Aurora Order rise to prominence. Colonization of the Southern Continent Post-1194 AE With the safe route established, the Great Powers of the North descend upon the Southern Continent. The already-fractured Balam Empire collapses as the Highlands Kingdom and Paz Kingdom fall to northern invasion. The continent is carved up between Loen and Intis, with Feysac also staking its claim. East Balam falls largely under Loen's control, while West Balam becomes a bloody battleground between Loen and Intis. The Kings of Loen adopt the title of Emperor of the Balam Empire to legitimize their rule. Plantations and manors spread across the land, and countless locals are enslaved or forced into servitude. The Orthodox Churches attempt to convert the population away from the faith of Death, but they find stiff resistance. The Numinous Episcopate, controlled by the Eggers Family, remains active, and faith in Death persists amongst the lower classes. The Psychology Alchemists are also founded around this time. Colonization of the Sonia Sea Pre- and Post-Roselle Even before Roselle's voyages, Northern nations had begun exploring the Sonia Sea. Loen had occupied Bansy Harbor roughly three hundred years prior and Damir Harbor over two hundred years ago. Within the last fifty years before the modern era, the Rorsted Archipelago is fully colonized by Loen. Formerly devoted to the Sea God Kalvetua, the islands are brought into the Loen fold. The Gargas Archipelago falls to the Feysac Empire. Power Balance Before the World War Late 13th–Early 14th Century AE By the eve of the World War, the Northern Continent is divided between five major powers, each backed by their own Orthodox Church and vast colonial holdings. Nation Main Orthodox Faiths Colonies / Holdings Loen Kingdom Church of the Evernight Goddess, Church of the Lord of Storms, Church of the God of Steam and Machinery East Balam, Rorsted Archipelago Feynapotter Kingdom Church of the Earth Mother West Balam (shared influence) Feysac Empire Church of the God of Combat West Balam, Sonia Island, Gargas Archipelago Intis Republic Church of the Eternal Blazing Sun West Balam, extensive trade network Republika of Lenburg (and allies) Church of the God of Knowledge and Wisdom Minor holdings, influential through knowledge and industry Old alliances are fraying, colonial disputes are constant, and the arms race fueled by steam technology brings the world closer to the brink with each passing year. World War c. 1349 AE (Novel Context) Tensions finally explode into a full-scale world war engulfing the Northern Continent. Old rivalries, colonial grudges, and the ambitions of great powers all converge into a conflict of unprecedented scale. The war is fought not only with rifles and cannons, but also with Beyonders. High-Sequence combatants turn the tide of battles, secret organizations sabotage their enemies from the shadows, and the influence of hidden cults grows with the chaos of war. By the time of the novel's opening, the war is still raging, casting a dark pall over the continent and further weakening the already frayed barrier against greater threats. Post-War 1349–1350 AE The war continues to grind on, exacting a horrific toll on all sides. Nations are drained of men and resources, industry is repurposed for weapons of war, and the common people suffer in the trenches and slums alike. Amidst this chaos, the veil between worlds grows thinner. More and more people are drawn into the world of mysticism, whether willingly or by force. The stage is set for the events of Lord of the Mysteries . Lord of Mysteries Year 1349 AE In the city of Tingen, in the Loen Kingdom, Zhou Mingrui awakens in the body of Klein Moretti . What begins as an attempt to survive in a strange world quickly spirals into a grand tapestry of conspiracy, divinity, and destiny. Through the Tarot Club and his own relentless pursuit of knowledge and strength, Klein navigates the treacherous waters of the Beyonder world, slowly uncovering the truth of Sefirah Castle, the history of the epochs, and the looming threat that hangs over all of reality. The Outer Deities' Invasion Approaching As the Fifth Epoch draws towards its later years, the pressure from beyond reality intensifies. The seals holding back the Outer Deities grow ever weaker, and their influence seeps into the world through dreams, madness, and Boons. Cults multiply, apocalyptic prophecies spread, and even the weakened Orthodox Gods find themselves struggling to hold back the tide. What was once distant whispers becomes an unavoidable reality—the Iron Age may well be the last age of humanity as it knows it.

title: First Epoch
summary: A spoiler-marked guide to the First Epoch of Lord of the Mysteries: the Lost Era, Era of Destruction, Era of Carnage, and the rise of the first Ancient God.
searchText: First Epoch World chronology · major spoilers First Epoch The Age of Chaos—from the lost history of Old Earth to the rise of the first Ancient God. The First Epoch is also called the Chaos Epoch or Age of Chaos. The source chronology divides it into the Lost Era, the Era of Destruction, and the Era of Carnage. It ends with the rise of Aurmir as the first Ancient God. Major spoilers for Lord of the Mysteries and related lore follow. Image Primary image from the Lord of Mysteries Wiki ↗ Epoch timeline The dates below are the epoch-local year ranges and durations used by the cited simplified chronology. The source leaves a one-year gap between the end of the Era of Destruction and the start of the Era of Carnage; this page preserves that wording rather than filling the gap. First Epoch periods and source chronology Era Epoch years Duration Key transition Lost Era 0–564 564 years Ends as the two Pillars’ convergence intensifies. Era of Destruction 564–566 2 years The First Blasphemy Slate forms after the Pillars’ war. Era of Carnage 567–981 414 years Aurmir’s rise as the first Ancient God ends the epoch. Each era name links to its corresponding row in the full world timeline . The reserved future-page target is kept on each row as data-page-target . Creation traditions Accounts passed down by the Orthodox Churches describe the Creator awakening from chaos, forming the world, and giving rise to the races and humanity. The City of Silver preserves a related creation tradition. These are inherited religious accounts, so they should be read separately from the article’s later section on “true history.” One recurring theme in these traditions is that the earliest beings were powerful and dangerous. Humanity’s place in the world is connected to the Creator’s intervention and to the return—or withdrawal—of power. Lost Era Years 0–564 The Lost Era is described as a period deliberately erased from history. On Old Earth, the Original Creator fully awakens, triggering an apocalypse that destroys most of humanity. A cataclysm reshapes the continents and seas, while the Creator’s internal fracture produces Sefirot, Uniquenesses, and Beyonder Characteristics. The Creator’s remains form a barrier that protects Earth from the Outer Deities. As Beyonder Characteristics spread among humans, animals, and surviving creatures, they contribute to the emergence and mutation of many races. The source also describes the Primordial God Almighty and the Celestial Worthy of Heaven and Earth for Blessings contesting control of the Sefirot. Their accommodation of additional Sefirot drives them beyond the stable limit of a Pillar and marks the end of the Lost Era. The detailed modern-world events and cosmological history are summarized from the source article; its cited chapters and author Q&A references are listed on the First Epoch source page . Era of Destruction Years 564–566 The Primordial God Almighty and the Celestial Worthy make arrangements related to their possible resurrections. The Son of Chaos is sealed inside the Magic Wishing Lamp and becomes the Genie. The Celestial Worthy and Primordial God Almighty then fight a full-scale war that extinguishes the sun and plunges the world into darkness. The source notes that the battle’s exact circumstances remain unknown. Both Pillars perish. The Primordial God Almighty’s corpse forms the First Blasphemy Slate in the Chaos Sea, with the Error Uniqueness beside it. The Celestial Worthy seals the other Sefirot to the Western Continent. The continent becomes isolated, and the Elves who left before the seal cannot return. Era of Carnage Years 567–981 As the world slowly recovers, Beyonder races lose the restraints imposed by the two Pillars. Madness and the instinct to converge fuel conflicts among the races and the kin of chaos, spreading violence across the land and seas. Omebella seeks to end the chaos. Zedus pursues the body bearing the Moon Uniqueness. Omebella eventually finds Aurmir guarding his parents’ remains and helps him regain some rationality. Zedus’s death and Aurmir’s birth as the first Ancient God—one not born from the Original Creator—mark the end of the First Epoch. At this point, the barrier’s countdown begins. ↑

searchText: Fool Pathway Lord of Mysteries · Standard Pathway Fool Pathway Sequence 9: Seer → Sequence 0: Fool The Fool Pathway, also called the Seer Pathway, centers on fooling perceptions and reality. It specializes in divination, illusions, appearance-changing, bodily control, and turning targets into marionettes through Spirit Body Threads; at high sequences it develops into historical summoning, miracles, concealment, and conceptual grafting. title: Fourth Epoch
summary: A spoiler-marked, detailed guide to the Fourth Epoch of Lord of the Mysteries: the Warring Era, Solomon Empire, Tudor-Trunsoest United Empire, Second Solomon Empire, War of the Four Emperors, Conflicts of the Seven Gods, and the Pale Era.
searchText: Fourth Epoch World chronology · major spoilers Fourth Epoch The Epoch of the Gods—an age of endless war, rising and falling empires, the ambitions of tyrants, and the slow descent into the Pale Era. Known as the Epoch of the Gods , the Fourth Epoch is the bloodiest and most chaotic age in human history. Born from the collapse of the Glorious Era, it is defined by constant warfare between the Orthodox Churches, the Solomon Empire's collapse, the rise of tyrannical emperors, the ambitions of the Four Horsemen, and the ever-growing desire for godhood. Throughout its entirety, the shadow of the Orthodox Gods looms over every conflict, with many seeking to usurp their thrones or replace them entirely. Major spoilers for Lord of the Mysteries and related lore follow. Epoch timeline The year ranges below follow the source-attributed simplified timeline used by the archive. The Fourth Epoch is divided into seven distinct eras, charting the continent's descent from the collapse of unity into a grim, lifeless age. Fourth Epoch periods and source chronology Era Epoch years BA range Duration Key transition Warring Era 0–112 2,582 BA – 2,470 BA 112 years Collapse of the Glorious Era; all-out war between Churches and factions. Solomon Empire 112–429 2,470 BA – 2,153 BA 317 years The Solomon Dynasty reclaims and rebuilds the empire amidst unrelenting conflict. Tudor-Trunsoest United Empire 429–581 2,153 BA – 2,001 BA 152 years The united rule of the Tudor and Trunsoest families sparks new ambition and strife. Second Solomon Empire 581–922 2,001 BA – 1,660 BA 341 years Restoration of Solomon rule, marked by growing instability and zealotry. War of the Four Emperors 922–979 1,660 BA – 1,603 BA 57 years Four titans vie for supremacy: Solomon, Tudor, Trunsoest and the Black Emperor. Conflicts of the Seven Gods 979–1192 1,603 BA – 1,390 BA 213 years The Orthodox Gods descend into open conflict, tearing the faiths apart. Pale Era 1192–1358 1,390 BA – 1,224 BA 166 years A dying age of ash, ruin, and the slow march towards the Fifth Epoch. Each era name links to its corresponding row in the full world timeline . The reserved future-page target is kept on each row as data-page-target . Overview More commonly referred to as the Epoch of the Gods , the Fourth Epoch is an age of unrestrained ambition. With God Almighty absent, the Seven Orthodox Gods no longer content themselves with merely guiding humanity. Many sought to expand their own authority, whilst mortals, fueled by the same ambition, sought to ascend beyond humanity and claim divinity for themselves. The Northern Continent is ripped apart by ceaseless war. Empires are forged overnight and crushed the next day. The title of "Emperor" is claimed by countless warlords, only for most to be drowned in a sea of blood. High-Sequence Beyonders become weapons of mass destruction, angelic wars are fought in the shadows of the material world, and the line between man and god grows thinner with each passing century. By its end, the continent is a broken husk, drained of life, faith, and hope. Warring Era Years 0–112 The Fourth Epoch begins with the collapse of the Glorious Era. The delicate balance maintained by God Almighty shatters the moment the Seven Orthodox Gods turn against one another and their followers. What was once inter-Church rivalry devolves into total war across the entire continent. The mighty Solomon Empire, already rotting from within, crumbles almost immediately. Its armies are pulled apart by civil war as provinces declare independence, nobles side with different Churches, and high-Sequence Beyonders carve out their own domains. The Orthodox Churches march under the banners of their gods, but their true goals are quickly revealed to be far more than just doctrinal supremacy. Each seeks to secure as much territory, as many Pathways, and as much authority as possible in the power vacuum left by God Almighty. This era of unrestrained slaughter lasts for over a century. By its end, there is nothing left of the unified continent. Ashen battlefields stretch from horizon to horizon, old nations are wiped off the map, and the people of the Northern Continent are left broken and desperate for any form of order, no matter how tyrannical. The Solomon Empire Years 112–429 Out of the fires of the Warring Era, a new Solomon Empire is established by the Solomon Dynasty. Claiming direct descent from the imperial family of the Third Epoch's Solomon Empire and carrying the banner of God Almighty, they rally the war-weary remnants of humanity under the promise of restoration, unity, and a return to the glory of old. For a time, it appears as though the dynasty may succeed where all others had failed. Through a combination of unmatched military might, the backing of several Orthodox Churches, and the leadership of terrifyingly powerful Beyonders, the new Solomon Empire manages to unify large swathes of the Northern Continent once more. Roads are rebuilt, order is restored in conquered lands, and the Church of the Eternal Blazing Sun rises to immense prominence under imperial patronage. However, history repeats itself. The Churches grow bolder with each passing year, refusing to be leashed by the throne. The nobility schemes incessantly, and the imperial family itself begins to be plagued by corruption and infighting. More importantly, many within the empire begin to fall victim to the same sin that brought down their predecessors: the desire for godhood. The seeds of rebellion are sown, and the empire slowly begins to rot from the inside once more. The Tudor-Trunsoest United Empire Years 429–581 The Solomon Empire's second collapse gives way to one of the Fourth Epoch's most infamous periods. The House of Tudor and the House of Trunsoest , two of the most powerful noble houses, forge an unprecedented alliance through marriage and conquest, establishing the Tudor-Trunsoest United Empire . This union would be defined by ambition on a scale never before seen. The Tudor family, in particular, would produce figures of terrifying talent and even more terrifying ambition. Most notable amongst them is Alista Tudor , who would rise through the ranks of mysticism at a blistering pace, eventually becoming known to history as the Blood Emperor . Under the United Empire, war reaches new heights of brutality. The Blood Emperor begins his meteoric ascent, slaughtering his way up the Sequence ladder whilst amassing a cult-like following of fanatical supporters. The empire expands rapidly through conquest, swallowing up the territories of rival factions with terrifying efficiency. However, the union between the two great houses is always tenuous at best. Jealousy, paranoia, and the lust for the throne fester behind closed doors. It is only a matter of time before the empire turns on itself. The United Empire would ultimately collapse under the weight of its own ambition, paving the way for yet another attempt at restoration. The Second Solomon Empire Years 581–922 Once more, a branch of the Solomon Dynasty manages to reclaim power, establishing the Second Solomon Empire . Determined not to repeat the mistakes of their predecessors, the new emperors rule with an iron fist, attempting to curb the power of both the nobility and the Churches with draconian measures. For a time, this iron rule brings about a period of brutal stability. However, the continent has changed far too much for such rule to last. The Churches have grown to be forces unto themselves, many powerful enough to challenge the empire directly. Countless secret orders dedicated to ascension have spread like weeds throughout the nobility and even within the imperial court itself. The empire becomes increasingly obsessed with the supernatural. The pursuit of godhood is no longer considered heresy by the radical factions within it, but a goal to be achieved. Black magic, forbidden rituals, and dealings with entities best left alone become commonplace amongst the upper echelons. The line between worshipping the Orthodox Gods and attempting to replace them grows impossibly thin. By the latter half of this era, the empire is a powder keg. Corruption is endemic, faith is fractured, and the most ambitious among the nobility are already plotting their own ascension to the throne of godhood. All that is needed is a spark to set the continent ablaze once more. The War of the Four Emperors Years 922–979 The spark comes in the form of open rebellion. Four titans of the era, each a powerhouse of terrifying might and each harbouring the ambition to become a god, rise up to claim dominion over the Northern Continent. History would come to know this conflict as the War of the Four Emperors . The four contenders are remembered as: The Solomon Emperor – The last true representative of the Solomon Dynasty, desperately clinging onto the legacy of his forebears and the hope of restoring the old order. The Tudor Emperor – A scion of House Tudor, carrying the burning ambition of the Blood Emperor within his bloodline. Many believe he seeks to complete what Alista Tudor started and claim the throne of God Almighty for himself. The Trunsoest Emperor – The ruler of the Trunsoest faction, cold, calculating, and backed by immense wealth, resources, and a terrifying host of high-Sequence Beyonders. The Black Emperor – The most mysterious and terrifying of the four. Wielding unfathomable power and leading an army of zealots, the Black Emperor marches with the explicit goal of overthrowing the entire Orthodox order and establishing a new, tyrannical rule of darkness. For fifty-seven years, the four clash in a war of unprecedented scale. Entire cities are reduced to rubble, angelic battles rip open the sky, and the Spiritual World encroaches onto the material plane with every major clash. The Orthodox Churches are dragged into the conflict, forced to pick sides or be crushed in the crossfire. Entire Pathways are on the verge of becoming derelict as their Beyonders are slaughtered en masse. By the end of the war, the Northern Continent is utterly devastated. The Second Solomon Empire is no more, the Tudor and Trunsoest factions are broken, and the Black Emperor stands triumphant over a sea of corpses. In the aftermath, the Black Emperor would establish his own reign, casting a long shadow over what is to come. Conflicts of the Seven Gods Years 979–1192 With the mortals having slaughtered one another to exhaustion, the true powers of the era can no longer remain idle. The Conflicts of the Seven Gods erupts as the Orthodox Gods themselves turn on each other in an open, apocalyptic war for supremacy. This is not a war fought solely through their clergy. Angels clash with Angels, divine kingdoms manifest in the Spirit World and Astral World, miracles are perverted into curses, and the very concept of faith is weaponized. Entire Churches are annihilated overnight, their holy sites razed, their gods' authority ripped away and seized by their rivals. The war is marked by countless betrayals, broken alliances, and acts of unspeakable blasphemy. Some gods attempt to usurp the authority of others, others desperately cling onto their domains, and a select few begin plotting to take the place of God Almighty himself. The faith of humanity is shattered. Many turn away from the gods entirely, whilst others become fanatical worshippers of whichever god is currently slaughtering the rest, desperate for salvation in a world gone mad. By the time the divine war comes to a halt, the Seven Orthodox Gods are all severely weakened. Their Churches lie in ruin, their authorities are fractured and contested, and the once unshakeable divine order is irrevocably broken. Never again would the Orthodox Gods be able to unite as they did during the Glorious Era. The age of divine unity is dead. Pale Era Years 1192–1358 The final era of the Fourth Epoch, the Pale Era , is aptly named. The Northern Continent has been reduced to a desolate wasteland. Great forests have been turned to ash, mighty cities lie in ruin, fertile lands have become barren, and an ever-present grey pall hangs over the sky. Many regions are completely devoid of life. The people that remain live in fear, huddling within crumbling walls, clinging onto the scraps of faith that they have left. With the Orthodox Gods too weak to enforce their will and the great empires all but destroyed, the continent descends into a state of feudal-like ruin. Warring lords, broken knight orders, heretical cults, and remnants of the ancient Churches all fight over the tiniest scraps of territory and resources. Mysticism is still practiced, but it is far more dangerous than ever before. The knowledge of the old age is being lost with every passing generation, locked away in crumbling libraries or hoarded by secretive orders on the brink of extinction. Faith has grown cold and lifeless. Prayers go unanswered more often than not. The name of God Almighty is rarely spoken with genuine hope anymore, only as a distant memory of a glory that will never return. Whispers of the Outer Deities grow louder in the desolate lands, and the seal placed upon them during ages past begins to grow thin once more. As the Pale Era draws to a close, the continent is quiet. An eerie, lifeless quiet. It is the calm before the storm. From the East, across the now-fractured world, the wheels of history begin to turn once more, heralding the coming of the Fifth Epoch —the modern age. ↑

title: Goddess of Fate
summary: The Goddess of Fate is one of the Outer Deities from the Cosmos that attempted to invade Earth.
searchText: Goddess of Fate Outer Deity Goddess of Fate Overview The Goddess of Fate is one of the Outer Deities from the Cosmos that attempted to invade Earth. "She" is the current owner of the Eternal Edict Pathway. "She" is the eldest daughter born from the union between the Mother Goddess of Depravity and the Original Creator. 1 Book 2, chapter 1168 Honorific Name The Weaver of All Fates; The Symbol of Ultimate Judgement; The Eternal Goddess of the Future (所有事物的命运纺织者， 最终裁决的象征， 永生的未来女神) Symbols, Authorities & Abilities "She" possesses full Authority over the Eternal Edict and the corresponding Symbols , which include but are not limited to the following: Eternal Edict: Authorities over the Weaving , Judgement , and Gathering of Fate. And the Symbols of Weaver of All Fates , Final Judgement and Eternal Life . 3 Book 2, chapter 1164 The Symbols , Authorities , and Abilities "She" possesses and displays at the Above the Sequence level include: Weaver of All Fates : "She" symbolizes the Weaving of chaotic destiny into a semblance of order, forming the foundation of the current River of Fate. 9 "She" can consciously Weave , guide, and sever even the fates of Great Old Dominators. 4 Book 2, chapter 1171 "She" can Weave a new Fate and new possibilities for "Herself" and others. 4 During Project Vortex, "She" blessed the event to be possible without being spied by other higher beings. 5 By using the bead relic originally belonging to a Dao Integrator of the Key of Light (Sefirah) as a medium, "She" could Weave a new Fate and grant new possibilities to the corresponding Dao Integrator inside the Golden Buddha, thus destabilizing "Him" and causing "His" body to collapse. 4 When facing the massive black hole created by the Supernova Dominator, "She" Wove "Her" own Fate to evade the pull and reach the edge of its influence unscathed. 4 The essence of Fate in the universe is infinite chaos. Even the Goddess of Fate can not fully control it, nor can "She" ensure the River of Fate always flows according to "Her" Woven designs. In the domain of arrangements, "She" is stronger than the God Almighty who wields authorities over the Mind and Envisioning . 10 Final Judgement : "She" is the symbol of Ultimate Judgement . "She" can cut others' River of Fate, severing all tributaries of Fate . By cutting, "She" can also indirectly affect the future and therefore affect dreams. 4 Those that are not Above the Sequence will watch helplessly as death and an end approaches them, with no way to reverse Fate . 6 Book 2, chapter 1172 For most Great Old Dominators, "They" will lose "Their" powers and authorities in such a state, unable to wield many of "Their" symbolisms. At that moment, a decisive attack from "Their" enemies can prove fatal. 6 The Final Judgment of Fate cannot directly kill a Great Old Dominator, but can temporarily strip "Them" of most of "Their" symbolisms, reducing "Them" to a weakened state because "They" are rejected by Fate itself. This rejection turns "Them" into miserable wretches with no future or dreams. 6 Eternal Life: As long as the Fates of all things converge into the River of Fate, "She" attains immortality as the Eternal Goddess of the Future . Even if "Her" body is destroyed, "Her" consciousness and spirit can return from the River of Fate and manifest a new body. 4 "She" does not need pre-set resurrection mechanisms or the reliance on undying spirits that other Great Old Dominators required, nor does "She" need to wait ages to revive through a Sefirah, Uniqueness, or Beyonder Characteristics. 4 "Her" return can be hindered if "Her" consciousness and spirit are Sealed after "Her" physical death. 5 The Lord of Mysteries and the Key of Light combined can perform a substitution at the level of Fate identity and status, to make someone ascend and take "Her" place. 7 Author's WeChat post sun_formulas, part 5 Countering Symbols, Authorities & Abilities Certain Symbols , Authorities , and Abilities of other Great Old Ones can counter some of "Her" powers, which include but are not limited to the following: Lord of Mysteries: 3 Theft, with the help of the Key of Light, counters Eternal Life . The Lord of Mysteries and the Key of Light combined can perform a substitution at the level of Fate identity and status, to make someone ascend and take "Her" place. 7 Beacon of Destiny mutually counters Weaver of All Fates . 11 Depending on the situation, the Goddess of Fate can counter the Lord of Mysteries' Beacon of Destiny ; a tug of war of symbolism where each counters the other and vice versa. In The Apocalypse, the Goddess of Fate was drawn in by the Lord of Mysteries Klein at the time 3 because "She" was a node of the current River of Fate, as such "She" would inevitably pass through the Beacon of Destiny . Foolishness counters Weaver of All Fates , which primarily centered on conscious manipulation on the domain of Fate . 12 Appearance True Form: "She" appeared with three bodies standing side by side, each in the form of a woman dressed in simple, elegant white dresses. The figure on the left had hollow eyes and skillfully wove silvery drops of destiny on an illusory loom into a net, that converged into stream. These streams flowed toward the middle body, which lacked arms, arriving at the present node of the River of Fate, merging into it and surging toward the void's edge. The figure on the right was headless, and held an illusory silver-black knife, cutting away portions of the River of Fate's tributaries. 2 Background According to the Seven Lights, ever since the Oldest One awakened and split apart, the most powerful Outer Deities in the entire universe gathered around this tiny solar system. Some of "Them" wish to retrieve "Their" Sefirot and characteristics that had been ripped from "Them", and were attracted here. Some of "Them" hope to get neighboring sefirot and high-level characteristics which "They" can accommodate. 8 Book 1, chapter 1271 The Goddess of Fate prioritized the Key of Light (Sefirah). If the Lord of Mysteries was defeated in a joint effort and Sefirah Castle was left vacant, "Her" goals would align with the Circle of Inevitability. As for the Chaos Sea and the associated the Uniqueness of White Tower and the Uniqueness of Visionary, there was a certain probability of "Her" interest. History On the first day, the Original Creator awoke and created this world, but Reality , the Spirit World , the Astral World , and Fate were still mixed together. On the second day, the Oldest One birthed the Mother Goddess of Depravity. Reality gained a foundation, the Spirit World and Astral World were separated, and the River of Fate began to flow. Soon after, the Mother Tree of Desire was born, giving rise to life and introducing evil and desire. Then came the Son of Chaos, who established order-and with it, shadows naturally emerged. 4 On the third day, the Oldest One and the Mother Goddess united, and the Mother of All Things gave birth to a firstborn daughter, the Goddess of Fate. From then on, the fates of all things began to intertwine, no longer in absolute chaos but instead forming relative patterns and foreseeable futures. 4 Before the First Epoch, the Circle of Inevitability and the Goddess of Fate frequently fought each other. 13 Even though the Mother Goddess of Depravity favored the Goddess of Fate, the reason why "She" didn't help "Her" was because the universe needed the Circle of Inevitability's Redemption Symbolism. 14 In the First Epoch, during the Lost Era, the Primordial God Almighty and Celestial Worthy's strong and still-perfect-and-whole power deterred the Outer Deities, who can only settle for observing Earth from afar for now. 15 Since 1352 of the Fifth Epoch, "She" is worshipped by the Dreamseekers on Earth. Their founder, Fate's Attendant Héloise, was responsible for weaving the entire matter during Project Vortex and ensuring it progressed smoothly without alerting higher beings and granting "blessing from fate", securing its success. 5 Book 2, chapter 865 In return Héloise acquired a thumb-sized bead with a glassy texture, radiating multicolored hues and naturally exuding a soothing aura that calmed the mind and body. This was an item that previously belonged to a Buddhist Kingdom of Light's Dao Integrator and was sacrificed to the Goddess of Fate after the transaction. 4 Trivia The Goddess of Fate might be a reference to the Moirai—often known in English as the Fates. In ancient Greek religion and mythology, the Moirai were the personifications of destiny. In certain accounts, they were considered as three sisters : Clotho (the spinner), Lachesis (the allotter), and Atropos (the inevitable, a metaphor for death). The Fates shape the destiny of each human, often expressed in textile metaphors such as spinning fibers into yarn, or weaving threads on a loom. References Book 2, chapter 1168. Book 2, chapter 1165. summary: Hanged Man Pathway: The Hanged Man Pathway represents Degeneration, while also framing sacrifice and responsibility positively. Its Above the Sequence is God
searchText: Hanged Man Pathway God Almighty · Standard Pathway Hanged Man Pathway Sequence 9: Secrets Suppliant → Sequence 0: Hanged Man The Hanged Man Pathway represents Degeneration, while also framing sacrifice and responsibility positively. Its Above the Sequence is God Almighty, and its corresponding Sefirah is the Chaos Sea. Pathway progression and late-sequence details contain major story spoilers. Browse the local Hanged Man Pathway ingredient archive → Sequence progression Sequence titles are retained from the archive; key ability notes are concise paraphrases of the linked source material. Seq. Name Key abilities 9 Secrets Suppliant High spiritual perception supports ritualistic magic, divination, aura detection, and dangerous knowledge of sacrifices. 8 Listener Listens directly to secret entities’ whispers, gaining distorted information while risking madness and shortened survival. 7 Shadow Ascetic Summons, curses, shapes, manipulates, and hides within shadows, with shadow weapons and risky summoned creatures. 6 Rose Bishop Uses flesh-and-blood magic for healing, bodily alteration, flesh servants, explosives, curses, and corrosive attacks. 5 Shepherd Grazes souls to borrow their Beyonder powers, switching among up to seven stored souls. 4 Black Knight Wields Cull of Spiritual Flesh, black armor, depraved-thought shadows, shadow commandeering, and externally released grazed souls. 3 Trinity Templar Uses Shadow Substitute, three-part flesh-and-blood bodies, regeneration, and simultaneous release of three grazed souls. 2 Profane Presbyter Weaponizes Profane Language to distort words, impose corruption or separation, curse targets, and deepen degeneration. 1 Dark Angel Controls the Shadow World, corrodes and betrays targets, weaponizes profane speech, manifests darkness, and commands dependent souls. 0 Hanged Man Embodies Sin-Bearing and Sacrifice while wielding partial authority over shadows, darkness, degeneration, filth, and mutation. Pathway themes & abilities Its core motifs are Sin-Bearing and Sacrifice, with partial authorities over Shadow, Darkness, Degeneration, Filth, and Mutation. Signature capabilities include ritualistic magic, listening to secret entities, shadow manipulation, flesh-and-blood magic, soul-grazing, profane words, corruption, mutation, and degeneration. Sequence-specific highlights are shown in the progression table above. High-sequence abilities The upper Sequences change the pathway from a specialist discipline into a domain of angelic and divine authority. The highlights below summarize the progression from Sequence 4 upward; details contain major spoilers. Sequences 4–3 Sequence 4 — Black Knight: Wields Cull of Spiritual Flesh, black armor, depraved-thought shadows, shadow commandeering, and externally released grazed souls. Sequence 3 — Trinity Templar: Uses Shadow Substitute, three-part flesh-and-blood bodies, regeneration, and simultaneous release of three grazed souls. Sequences 2–1 Sequence 2 — Profane Presbyter: Weaponizes Profane Language to distort words, impose corruption or separation, curse targets, and deepen degeneration. Sequence 1 — Dark Angel: Controls the Shadow World, corrodes and betrays targets, weaponizes profane speech, manifests darkness, and commands dependent souls. Sequence 0 Sequence 0 — Hanged Man: Embodies Sin-Bearing and Sacrifice while wielding partial authority over shadows, darkness, degeneration, filth, and mutation. Sequence highlights are paraphrased from the Lord of the Mysteries Wiki pathway article . Novel lore & story appearances Major spoilers for Lord of the Mysteries and Circle of Inevitability . The Hanged Man pathway is framed not only by degeneration but by sin-bearing and sacrifice, giving its symbolism a narrative echo in the True Creator’s origin: after the Ancient Sun God’s fall, the betrayed god’s remnants—including the Hanged Man uniqueness and degeneration authority—contributed to the True Creator’s rebirth. The Aurora Order, whose primary pathway is Hanged Man, worships him; its plot to bring his spawn into the world drives the Tingen catastrophe, and it later participates in the Great Smog of Backlund. In the later Utopia crisis, Adam’s alliance with Zaratul puts Klein in Adam’s Corpse Cathedral Story connections Origin and betrayal: the Rose Redemption’s betrayal and the Ancient Sun God’s death precede the True Creator’s emergence from the remains; his rebirth is specifically tied to Hanged Man characteristics and degeneration authority Aurora Order plots: the Order worships the True Creator and primarily uses the Hanged Man pathway; it is implicated in both the Tingen spawn incident and the Great Smog of Backlund Utopia and Adam: Adam helps Zaratul enter Klein’s Utopia; after Klein is isolated from Sefirah Castle, he is taken to Adam’s Corpse Cathedral and learns more of Adam’s identity Alger’s namesake and change: Alger is initially a Tyrant/Sailor-pathway Beyonder whose Tarot Club codename is the Hanged Man; by the end of Book Two he has switched to the actual Hanged Man pathway Figures to know Ancient Sun God the source from whose death and remains the True Creator emerged True Creator the Hanged Man pathway’s Sequence 0 deity and Aurora Order’s object of worship Adam Ancient Sun God’s divinity-side figure; later fuses with the True Creator and intervenes in Klein’s Utopia advancement crisis Alger Wilson Tarot Club’s Hanged Man, later an actual Hanged Man-pathway angel after switching from Tyrant Major story spoilers. Paraphrased from the Fandom pathway article .. Complete wiki information Full main-article information imported from the Hermit Pathway wiki article . Existing archive pathway details above are preserved. The Mystery Pryer pathway is different from other pathways. From time to time, it will be chased by a large amount of knowledge. It’s impossible to ignore, and there’s no way to reject it even if one can’t handle it. And when one consumes a potion to advance, the situation of being chased by knowledge becomes even more serious. Aurore to Lumian Lee On Circle of Inevitability , Chapter 48 Overview The Hermit Pathway seems to specialize in knowledge of the mystical and occult world. They have good ritual magic abilities, cast various spells and make scrolls with corresponding materials, as well as conjure and manipulate stars. At High-Sequences, they can see and hear hidden existences easily, extract powers from mystical knowledge, and foresee the woven of fate; they become information themselves; they can modify their bodies, bring power to knowledge, instill knowledge upon the minds of others, and manipulate the symbolisms of number, thus bring all sorts of strong and terrifying effects. The pathway was controlled by the Hidden Sage , which often makes the situation of Beyonders of this pathway tragic as "He" routinely whispers knowledge into their ears, especially during their Sequence advancement. Failing to assimilate the knowledge will either turn you into a raving lunatic or an outright monster . According to Aurore , 99% of the Knowledge Pursuit comes from the Hidden Sage. [ 2 ] [ 3 ] "He" doesn't have a ridiculous level of malicious intent towards members of the Moses Ascetic Order , it is relatively safe for them to listen to "Him," but even Cattleya who is one of them would have lost control if The Fool didn't save her. [ 4 ] The Above the Sequence of the Hermit Pathway is the Demon of Knowledge , and the corresponding Sefirah is the Knowledge Moor . title: High-Dimensional Overseer
summary: The High-Dimensional Overseer is one of the Outer Deities from the Cosmos that attempted to invade Earth.
searchText: High-Dimensional Overseer Outer Deity High-Dimensional Overseer Overview The High-Dimensional Overseer is one of the Outer Deities from the Cosmos that attempted to invade Earth. "He" is the current owner of the Sublunary Eye Pathway. Honorific Name The Lord of Dimensions; The Eye Overlooking the Mortal Realm; The Source of All Illusions; The Creator of the Painting World (维度之主， 俯视尘世的眼睛， 一切幻想的源头， 画中世界的造物主) TRANSLATION NOTE The " Sublunary " (Chénshì) in "Sublunary Eye" (Chénshì zhī yǎn) is the same Chinese word as the " Mortal Realm " in "The Eye Overlooking the Mortal Realm" (Fǔshì chénshì de yǎnjīng) A closer translation to " The Source of All Illusions " (一切幻想的源头) from the official Webnovel English translation is " The Source of All Fantasies " instead. Symbols, Authorities & Abilities TRANSLATION NOTE In the original Chinese text, 真理 (zhēnlǐ) and 真实 (zhēnshí) are distinct terms with different nuances, though both can be translated as “Truth” in English, as is done in the English WebNovel translation (School of Truth and the symbolism of Truth respectively). This note will illustrate the different meanings lost in translation. Chaos Mist's Truth (真理, zhēnlǐ): Universal Truth; It denotes a universal, objective, or philosophical truth that reflects the fundamental principles of reality, often absolute or unchanging. Sublunary Eye's Truth (真实, zhēnshí): Truth/Reality; It denotes factual existence, genuineness, or something that is not false or illusory, often concrete and verifiable. "He" possesses full Authority over the Sublunary Eye and the corresponding Symbols , which include but are not limited to the following: Sublunary Eye: Authorities, and the Symbols of Dimensionality and Truth . 1 This Pathway is a mix of two different Pathways: 7 The Pathway of Dimension . The Sequence 0 name is Sublunary Eye. 8 The Pathway of Fantasy . The Symbols , Authorities , and Abilities "He" possesses and displays at the Above the Sequence level include: '''Dimensionality ( Wéidù) : As the Lord of Dimensions ( Wéidù zhī zhǔ) , "He" can freely traverse through Higher and Lower Dimensions and affect the Dimensionality''' of other beings. 2 "He" can counter abilities such as Parasitism , Marionettes , and Blink of the Lord of Mysteries. 2 From higher and lower Dimensions , Spirit Body Threads are tangible and real-something that could be touched. Blink only allowed movement on a small scale, while those Parasitized were bound together into one entity. "He" can swiftly ascend to the tenth Dimension to directly disrupt the internal connections of the aggregate forms of the Celestial Master and the Celestial Thearch. 3 Book 2, chapter 1168 "He" can trap others into lower Dimensions . Under "His" gaze, the Celestial Master rapidly thinned, becoming a paper figurine and melding into the surrounding scenery as part of a Painting . 1 "He" can ascend Dimensions to instantly move away from the Galaxy "He" is currently in. 9 '''Truth ( Zhēnshí) : "He" wields the symbolism of Truth''', being able to see the true state of things and through obstructions. "He" is unaffected by the Calamity of Destruction's Fog of War . 1 Book 2, chapter 1166 "He" is able to see through Deceit from a higher Dimension and locate the position of a transferred object. 10 "He" can see through the Truth , and discover the weaknesses within the states of existences. "He" saw the weaknesses within the aggregate forms of the Celestial Master and the Celestial Thearch from a Higher Dimension . 3 This is an ability of the Fantasy Pathway. 11 '''The Creator of the Painting World ( Huà zhōng shìjiè de zàowùzhǔ)''': "He" can unfurl the illusory, coiled Strings around "Him" to form a Dimensional Painting that's filled with suns, planets, and a variety of rules and principles. 3 By setting the exit in a concealed location, this can trap both the Celestial Master and the Celestial Thearch for some time. 3 Beings in Higher Dimensions or within "His" Dimensional Painting will not be fully consumed by the explosion of Desires from the Father of Devils, "They" would only enter a brief state of stagnation. 12 Within "His" Paintings , "He" is Omnipotent and Omniscient . 13 The maximum possible power level of a creature created or summoned by "His" abilities is close to Sequence 0. 14 Countering Symbols, Authorities & Abilities Certain Symbols , Authorities , and Abilities of other Great Old Ones can counter some of "His" powers, which include but are not limited to the following: Lord of Mysteries: Change and Dimensionality in one-on-one scenario mutually counteracts each other. King of Space-Time could hinder the Lord of Dimensions from freely traversing dimensions. Demon of Knowledge: Information is widespread and all-encompassing in hierarchy. It is not restricted by lower Dimensions . Humans are conglomerations of Information , and Paintings are as well. 1 The Celestial Master turned incorporeal, transforming into a torrent of complex and massive Information to break free of the confines of the High-Dimensional Overseer's Painting . 1 However, when the High-Dimensional Overseer escaped to the highest dimension, the Celestial Master could only have minimal influence on this domain. 4 Book 2, chapter 1176 The Anarchy / Son of Chaos: The Celestial Thearch can order all Dimensions — higher, lower, and the current one — to become interconnected, as though overlaid with layer upon layer of glass barriers. As a result, the High-Dimensional Overseer could no longer increase dimensions unscathed, nor could the Celestial Thearch's dimensions be lowered without maintaining "His" influence on the battlefield. However, when the High-Dimensional Overseer escaped to the highest dimension, the Celestial Thearch could only have minimal influence on this domain. 4 Eternal Darkness: Pallor , which restrains colors, would have a strong restraining effect against the Painting World . 15 Appearance True Form : An untouchable shadow from a higher dimension. Has a pair of indifferent, clear, and emotionless eyes, as if containing the entire universe. 16 17 Background According to the Seven Lights, ever since the Oldest One awakened and split apart, the most powerful Outer Deities in the entire universe, including the High-Dimensional Overseer, gathered around this tiny solar system. Some of "Them" wish to retrieve "Their" Sefirot and Beyonder Characteristics that had been ripped from "Them", and were attracted here. Some of "Them" have the hope of getting neighboring Sefirot and high-level characteristics which "They" can accommodate. 18 High-Dimensional Overseer desired Sefirot related to rules, order, and space-time. Through divination and prophecy, Klein deduced that "He" sought either the Nation of Disorder or the River of Eternal Darkness. If the Great Old Dominators concentrated "Their" efforts on pressing the Lord of Mysteries back into "His" coffin, the High-Dimensional Overseer would also likely seek to accommodate the the Uniqueness of Door and the Uniqueness of Error, and take control of Sefirah Castle. 2 Book 2, chapter 1164 History As of 1358 of the Fifth Epoch, the High-Dimensional Overseer and "His" followers had been relatively passive, avoiding bloodshed and not frequently engaging in sacrificial rituals. Even if they did, it was usually confined to themselves and those in their immediate vicinity, minimizing the danger. 5 Book 2, chapter 448 However, they were not as ‘harmless’ as previously believed and the threat they posed was revealed when The Hostel, a ritual conducted using powers of the Sublunary Eye Pathway, commenced. 5 During Project Vortex, the medium via which the Outer Deities' power breached the barrier, the Endless Cosmos oil painting, was created by Sage as per the wishes of the High-Dimensional Overseer. 19 During The Apocalypse, "He" fought against the quasi-Great Old Ones from Earth, mainly the Celestial Master and the Celestial Thearch. Trivia Termiboros once claimed to have knowledge about this Outer Deity but refused to elaborate further. 5 The High-Dimensional Overseer and Monarch of Decay can devour each other; If one of "Them" succeeds and further accommodates the Uniqueness of Door, "They" can attain the King of Space-Time symbolism. 20 Translations Language Name Chinese 高维俯视者 Thai ผู้ทอดมมองจากเบื้องบน References Book 2, chapter 1166. title: History of the World
summary: A spoiler-marked guide to the history of the Lord of the Mysteries world, from its creation through the Five Epochs, with a source-attributed timeline table.
searchText: History of the World World chronology · major spoilers History of the World From the first three days to the Iron Age: a guide to the eras, powers, and turning points that shaped the world. This page brings together a short history-by-era overview and the relative-year timeline currently available in the source article. The numbered chronology is presented as reported there; it is not an attempt to fill gaps or reconcile every uncertainty in the lore. This page contains major spoilers for Lord of the Mysteries and references to Circle of Inevitability . Relative-year timeline The source table uses Year 1349 of the Fifth Epoch—the year Zhou Mingrui arrives as Klein Moretti —as its novel-start reference point. “BA” means “Before Arrival.” The epoch-year range is local to the epoch named in the first column. The published table in the cited article covers the First through Fourth Epochs and ends with the Pale Era. Fifth Epoch events are summarized below, but a complete Fifth Epoch range is not supplied in that table. Relative dates and era lengths as listed in the source timeline Epoch Era or period Relative to novel start Relative to current epoch Duration Start End Start End First Epoch Lost Era 7,210 BA 6,646 BA 0 564 564 years Era of Destruction 6,646 BA 6,644 BA 564 566 2 years Era of Carnage 6,643 BA 6,229 BA 567 981 414 years Second Epoch Sprouting Era 6,229 BA 4,961 BA 0 1,268 1,268 years Early Era of Fire 4,961 BA 4,499 BA 1,268 1,730 462 years Dual Era 4,499 BA 4,269 BA 1,730 1,960 230 years Era of Tranquility 4,269 BA 3,904 BA 1,960 2,325 365 years Dawn Era 3,904 BA 3,668 BA 2,325 2,561 236 years Third Epoch Glorious Era 3,668 BA 2,582 BA 0 1,086 1,086 years Fourth Epoch Warring Era 2,582 BA 2,470 BA 0 112 112 years Solomon Empire 2,470 BA 2,186 BA 112 396 284 years Tudor-Trunsoest United Empire 2,186 BA 2,072 BA 396 510 114 years Second Solomon Empire 2,072 BA 1,535 BA 510 1,047 537 years War of the Four Emperors 1,535 BA 1,530 BA 1,047 1,052 5 years Conflicts of the Seven Gods 1,530 BA 1,372 BA 1,053 1,210 157 years Pale Era 1,372 BA 1,349 BA 1,210 1,233 23 years Fifth Epoch Iron Age 1,349 BA Present 0 — Ongoing Every era row keeps a stable anchor for quick reference within the timeline. The beginning and Pre-Epoch The first three days On the first day, the Original Creator awakens and creates the world. Reality, the Spirit World, the Astral World, and Fate are not yet fully separated. On the second day, the Oldest One gives birth to the Mother Goddess of Depravity ; the foundations of Reality are established, the Spirit and Astral Worlds separate, and the River of Fate begins to flow. The Mother Tree of Desire and the Son of Chaos also emerge, bringing desire and order—and, in their wake, corruption and shadows. On the third day, the Oldest One and the Mother Goddess unite. The Mother of All Things gives birth to the Goddess of Fate , after which the fates of beings begin to form patterns and more foreseeable futures instead of remaining in absolute chaos. Pre-Epoch After creating the universe, the Original Creator falls asleep. Personalities such as Primordial God Almighty and the Celestial Worthy of Heaven and Earth for Blessings form from the slumbering Creator and begin to influence reality indirectly through their authorities and Beyonder Characteristics. A cataclysm around the modern era destroys the old world; the Survivors and Transmigrators originate from that period. First Epoch: The Age of Chaos Read the full guide → The First Epoch’s exact start and end are unknown. Its early world is described as dark, chaotic, and mad. As the Beyonder races gradually regain reason, the First Blasphemy Slate appears. The Western Continent disappears into the gray fog. Second Epoch: The Dark Epoch Read the full guide → As Beyonder Characteristics are purified, the major races develop civilizations and eight Ancient Gods rise one after another, ruling the sky, land, oceans, Spirit World, and Astral World. Humanity struggles under stronger races—including Giants, Elves, and Sanguines—until the Ancient Sun God awakens and takes back authorities from the Ancient Gods. Humanity then rises in revolt. Third Epoch: The Glorious Era Read the full guide → Following humanity's revolt at the end of the Second Epoch, Adam—known as God Almighty and the Ancient Sun God—unifies the continent and establishes the Orthodox Churches. The Solomon Empire rises to unprecedented glory, codifying the Pathway system under divine order. As God Almighty grows distant, ambition festers amongst the gods and mortals alike, eventually collapsing the age into war. Fourth Epoch: The Epoch of the Gods Read the full guide → The Fourth Epoch is born from the collapse of the Glorious Era. Warring Churches, rising and falling empires, the Blood Emperor, the War of the Four Emperors, and the Conflicts of the Seven Gods reduce the Northern Continent to ruin. It ends in the desolate Pale Era, on the brink of the Fifth Epoch. Fifth Epoch: The Iron Age Read the full guide → In the Northern Continent, the seven Orthodox Churches and Four Great Nations shape public life while secret organizations operate in the shadows. In the Southern Continent, resistance movements and kingdoms—including the Highland Kingdom and Paz Kingdom—rise before northern invasions destroy them. Roselle Gustav’s arrival and improvements to the steam engine accelerate industrialization, steamship travel, piracy, and colonial expansion. A world war engulfs the nations of the Northern Continent. As the barrier weakens, the Outer Deities press against reality, and Boon Recipients grow more numerous, placing the world in greater danger. ↑
